items.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020
items.q: Ellis helped launch the careers of Harry Connick Jr.

ctx.x: Pianist and educator Ellis Marsalis was born in New Orleans in 1934. He has performed and recorded with a diverse list of artists, including Al Hirt, Cannonball Adderley and Kermit Ruffins. Ellis taught extensively at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts and helped launch the careers of Harry Connick Jr., Terrance Blanchard and Nicholas Payton. He has recorded as a leader and with his sons, Wynton, Branford, Delfeayo and Jason.
Ellis was interviewed in New Orleans, Louisiana on January 7, 2020 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Contrary to that, when you get the kind of support, especially parental support, which you get as a kid with a lot of talent, both parents are very supportive of him, then you get a Harry Connick, Jr. His parents are very supportive.

ctx.x: How early did he manifest this ability? It must have been . . . .

He could – it was like somebody as a kid who could fix anything, music or otherwise. He did manifest it at a young age. The 12 years that I spent at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts, I don’t want to say that I was bitter, because I wasn’t, but I realized during those 12 years that the whole thing of talent is misconstrued by most people. I don’t necessarily mean coming up with a definition of it. I saw so many kids who came through and had serious talent. They either fell by the wayside with some drugs or…

We never did discourage our kids from playing, and like I said, I was always – always was able to find somebody who could teach the instrument and knew what they were doing. Unlike medicine, anybody can hang out a shingle and say “music teacher” and don’t go to jail.
